text: small R package visualizing linear models. Plots anything simple lines high-dimensional squiggles functions. Start fitting lm(), hand Applr. what: geom_slice(): your model as a ggplot2 layer
title: Visualize and Explain Linear Models
text: geom_slice() draws prediction line fitted lm() across plot (facets). looks like geom_smooth(), geom_smooth() fits model plotted data, geom_slice() draws model fitted. main driver autoplot.lm, makes decisions possible. move beyond single predictor, geom_slice() creates 2d “slice” (slices) high-dimensional model. predictors held constants, showing slice model looking . don’t specify values, geom_slice() make guess follows: Variables named predict_vars held chosen values. Variables mapped grouping aesthetic (aes(color = g)) held group’s value - one line per group. Facet variables held panel’s value. Anything left imputed (mean numeric, common value factors), console message naming value used. everything, console messages labeling helpers try make model clear possible - know exactly looking . example, fitted model 4 predictors can’t plotted line without making multiple assumptions. console messages clarify decisions make order plot 2d slice.  assumptions made, can make better ones. plot shows model far clearer utilizing several features geom_slice() offers.
code: set.seed(123) n <- 80 x <- runif(n, 0.1, 10) x2 <- runif(n, 0.1, 10) x3 <- sample(c(1, 20, 40), n, replace = TRUE) x4 <- sample(c(1, 2), n, replace = TRUE) y <- log(5 + x + x2 + x3 + 1/5 * x * x3 + 80 * x4) # no random noise dat <- data.frame(x, x2, x3, x4, y)  model <- lm(exp(y) ~ x*x3 + x2 + x4, data = dat)   # exact model fit  # What geom_slice will do on its own (minimum inference) ggplot(dat, aes(x, y)) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model) +   labs(title = "A Perfectly Fit Model 'Slice'") #> Value for `x3` not specified - Used mean: 19.36 #>     To choose a slice, use 'predict_vars = list(x3 = 19.36)'. #> Value for `x2` not specified - Used mean: 4.981 #>     To choose a slice, use 'predict_vars = list(x2 = 4.981)'. #> Value for `x4` not specified - Used mean: 1.412 #>     To choose a slice, use 'predict_vars = list(x4 = 1.412)'. #> Predictions of `exp(y)` were back-transformed to match the `y` axis. #>     To turn this off, use 'back_transform = FALSE'.  # Shows the model is an exact fit (and geom_slice can plot axis transforms) ggplot(dat, aes(x = log(5 + x + x2 + x3 + 1/5 * x * x3 + 80 * x4), y)) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model) +   labs(title = "Same Model, Different X-Axis") #> Predictions of `exp(y)` were back-transformed to match the `y` axis. #>     To turn this off, use 'back_transform = FALSE'. ggplot(dat, aes(x, y, color = factor(x3))) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model, band = "x2", predict_vars = list(x2 = c(0, 10))) +   facet_wrap(~x4) +   geom_slice_text() +   geom_slice_subtitle()

text: Writes label end slice line; especially useful band multiple predict_vars specified.     Options: style ("variable" writes "hp: 66", "value" writes bare values, "legend" adds corner key), location = "left"/"right", offset, color.
code: model <- lm(Sepal.Length ~ Sepal.Width + Petal.Length, iris)  ggplot(iris, aes(Petal.Length, Sepal.Length)) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model, band = TRUE) +   geom_slice_text() set.seed(123)  n <- 80 x <- runif(n, -10, 10) x2 <- runif(n, 0, 4) g <- factor(sample(c("A", "B"), n, replace = TRUE)) y <- x * ifelse(g == "A", 0.5, 2) + ifelse(g == "A", 5, -5) + 4 * x2 + rnorm(n) dat <- data.frame(x, g, y) model <- lm(y ~ x * g + x2, data = dat)  # labels auto-color ggplot(dat, aes(x, y, color = g)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +   geom_slice(model, predict_vars = list(x2 = c(0, 2, 4))) +   geom_slice_text() # Multiple predictors represent one line ggplot(dat, aes(x, y)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +   geom_slice(model, predict_vars = list(x2 = c(0, 2, 4), g = c("A", "B"))) +   geom_slice_text() # Identical, with `style = "legend"` ggplot(dat, aes(x, y)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +   geom_slice(model, predict_vars = list(x2 = c(0, 2, 4), g = c("A", "B"))) +   geom_slice_text(style = "legend")

text: Low-level ggproto objects power geom_slice(). users never need call directly, can custom layers. Note StatSlice reads aesthetic mapping params — geom_slice() supplies automatically, raw layer() call must pass explicitly:
code: library(ggplot2) model <- lm(mpg ~ disp + hp + cyl, data = mtcars)  ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   layer(stat = StatSlice,         geom = GeomSlice,         position = "identity",         inherit.aes = TRUE,         params = list(model = model, predict_vars = list(hp = 110),                       mapping = aes(disp, mpg)))

title: Write out the equation of a linear model — lm_equation
code: # Simple regression lm_equation(lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)) #> [1] "mpg = 37.3 - 5.34*wt"  # Multiple predictors lm_equation(lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars)) #> [1] "mpg = 30.7 - 0.0303*disp - 0.0248*hp"  # Factor predictor: one term per non-reference level, spelled out by default model <- lm(Sepal.Length ~ Sepal.Width + Species, data = iris) lm_equation(model) #> [1] "Sepal.Length = 2.25 + 0.804*Sepal.Width + 1.46*(Species=\"versicolor\") + 1.95*(Species=\"virginica\")"  # `style = "brackets"` shows just the level; `"raw"` keeps design-matrix names lm_equation(model, style = "brackets") #> [1] "Sepal.Length = 2.25 + 0.804*Sepal.Width + 1.46*[versicolor] + 1.95*[virginica]" lm_equation(model, style = "raw") #> [1] "Sepal.Length = 2.25 + 0.804*Sepal.Width + 1.46*Speciesversicolor + 1.95*Speciesvirginica"  # Transformed terms and interactions lm_equation(lm(mpg ~ wt + I(wt^2), data = mtcars)) #> [1] "mpg = 49.9 - 13.4*wt + 1.17*I(wt^2)" lm_equation(lm(Sepal.Length ~ Sepal.Width * Species, data = iris)) #> [1] "Sepal.Length = 2.64 + 0.69*Sepal.Width + 0.901*(Species=\"versicolor\") + 1.27*(Species=\"virginica\") + 0.175*Sepal.Width:(Species=\"versicolor\") + 0.211*Sepal.Width:(Species=\"virginica\")"  # No-intercept models print no intercept lm_equation(lm(mpg ~ 0 + wt, data = mtcars)) #> [1] "mpg = 5.29*wt"
